title: Garden and Wolf
premise: Sebastian Montrose, the last guide of the fading Wayfarers' Guild, has spent her life invisible—until a dying courier presses a dragon-scale map into her hands and breathes her final words: 'Carry it to the Ember.' The map marks the hidden roost of the last dragons, and both the Crown's inquisitors and the resurrected Order of the Ashen Blade will kill to claim it. Hunted through the Thornfells, Sebastian gathers an unlikely found family—a disgraced knight, a runaway scribe, and a half-dragon child—and learns the guild's oldest secret: the Wayfarers were founded as dragon-wardens, not smugglers. In the end, she chooses justice over survival, exposing the Order's false war before the assembled mountain clans, and carries the dying ember of dragon-fire into a new age where she is finally, unmistakably seen.
about_author: Ansel Amberdale is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping remote mountain passes before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about borders, belonging, and the people who live in the spaces maps forget.

chapters.title: The Last Wayfarer
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. On a routine smuggling run through Thornfell, Sebastian guides a merchant caravan past a burned-out waystation, quietly mourning the guild's decline. She returns to a guildhall with three members left. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence; she prefers roads to people.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Door
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. A bloodied woman collapses at the guildhall door during a storm, pressing a scale-patterned map into Sebastian's hands and whispering 'the Ember' before dying. The guildmaster orders the body buried and the map burned. Beat: dread—the moment invisibility ends.

chapters.title: What the Map Burns
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. The map refuses to burn; instead it glows when Sebastian's blood touches it, revealing paths no chart shows. That night, inquisitors arrive asking about a missing courier. Beat: fear sharpening into defiance as she hides the map instead of surrendering it.

chapters.title: Ashes on the Road
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Fleeing ahead of the inquisitors, Sebastian takes the old guild roads alone but finds them watched. She rescues Corwin, a disgraced knight left to die in a ravine by the Ashen Blade, who recognizes the map and begs to help. Beat: reluctant alliance born of mutual shame.

chapters.title: The Scribe Who Read Too Much
chapters.summary: POV Wren (runaway scribe). Wren, hiding from the Order she once copied decrees for, deciphers fragments of the map: it points to the Ember Roost, cradle of the last dragons. She catches up to Sebastian and trades knowledge for passage. Beat: cautious hope—two liars recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Ghosts of the Guild
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Sheltering in a ruined waystation, Sebastian finds her grandmother's journal among abandoned guild records: the Wayfarers were dragon-wardens, sworn to guard the roost, until a betrayal ended the covenant. Beat: grief transmuting into inheritance—she was never just a smuggler.

chapters.title: The Child in the Hollow
chapters.summary: POV Corwin. In a cave system, the trio discovers Pip, a half-dragon child hunted by the Order, who can hear the map humming. Corwin, who once executed innocents for the Order, vows this time he'll protect. Beat: redemption taking its first real step.

chapters.title: Inquisitor Vane
chapters.summary: POV antagonist (Vane). The Order's chief inquisitor interrogates the guildmaster, learning Sebastian lives. Vane believes dragons are abominations and their fire must be extinguished to prevent war. Beat: chilling conviction—an enemy who thinks she is the hero.

chapters.title: Crossing the Weeping Stair
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. A treacherous ascent nearly kills Pip; Sebastian abandons the safe route to save her, burning days of lead time. Wren accuses her of sentiment; Sebastian answers that the guild serves travelers, not schedules. Beat: found family crystallizing under pressure.

chapters.title: The Village That Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Wren. In a highland village, elders recognize the map and tell of the Night of Cinders, when the Order burned the roost's outer eyries. Villagers shelter the group but one boy runs to sell them out. Beat: warmth shadowed by betrayal; history is alive here.

chapters.title: Blade in the Snow
chapters.summary: POV Corwin. Ambushed by his former brothers-in-arms, Corwin duels his old commander to buy escape and takes a wound that won't close cleanly. He confesses his crimes to Sebastian. Beat: guilt laid bare; trust tested and, surprisingly, kept.

chapters.title: The False War
chapters.summary: POV Vane. Vane stages a dragon attack on a border town using captured wyvern-fire, manufacturing public terror to justify a crusade into Thornfell. Beat: rising stakes—the enemy isn't chasing a map anymore; she's building an army.

chapters.title: Ember Road
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Following the map's living glow, the group crosses into a hidden valley where the air is warm and ancient waystones hum. Pip begins to change—scales brightening, senses opening. Beat: awe; the destination feels like a memory returning.

chapters.title: The Last Dragon
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. They meet Ysolde, the last true dragon, ancient and guttering, who tests each traveler with their own truths. She reveals the map chose Sebastian because her blood carries the warden covenant. Beat: identity confronted—she cannot refuse what she is.

chapters.title: Covenant Refused
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. Overwhelmed, Sebastian tries to hand the burden to Corwin or Wren; Ysolde lets her walk away. Alone on a ridge, Sebastian realizes every road she ever took was practice for this one. Beat: dark night of the soul turning toward acceptance.

chapters.title: The Roost Falls
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Vane's army breaches the valley using the betrayed boy's knowledge. Wren races to warn the roost while Corwin holds a pass nearly single-handedly. Beat: sacrifice and urgency; everything they built is burning.

chapters.title: Fire and Judgment
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. At the climax, Sebastian stands between Vane's army and the dying dragon, invoking the warden covenant before the gathered mountain clans Vane needs as allies. She exposes the staged attack with Wren's stolen Order documents. Beat: courage—justice spoken aloud, outside any law but her own.

chapters.title: Vane's Last Argument
chapters.summary: POV Vane. Unmasked, Vane attempts to kill Ysolde herself; Pip, fully awakened, shields the dragon, and Vane falls to her own consumed fire. Beat: catharsis—the zealot destroyed by the hatred she fed.

chapters.title: What the Fire Costs
chapters.summary: POV Corwin. Ysolde gives her remaining flame to rekindle the covenant stones, dimming toward her final sleep. Corwin, wounded, survives long enough to see the clans swear new wardens. Beat: bittersweet victory; endings that make beginnings possible.

chapters.title: The Rekindled Guild
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. The Wayfarers' guildhall reopens—not for smuggling, but as a warden school with Sebastian as its youngest-ever master, Wren as chronicler, Corwin as arms-master. Beat: homecoming; the family becomes an institution.

chapters.title: Eggs in the Deep
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Exploring the roost's deepest vaults, they find dormant eggs Ysolde guarded all along—hope she never spoke of. Pip, now the first warden-dragon, begins teaching them to wake. Beat: wonder restored; the future is larger than feared.

chapters.title: Every Road Leads Home
chapters.summary: POV Sebastian. A year later, Sebastian guides her first students through Thornfell, pausing at the grave of the stranger who started it all. She leaves a waystone marked with the covenant sigil. Final beat: the invisible girl made visible—identity, justice, and family all carried home.
